sm: P. Andrew Sandlin responds to the recent derisive use of the phrase propositional nation, meaning a country founded on truths or principles binding on citizens and leaders, as opposed to a kinship community based on race, ethnicity, land, language and ancestry. He ties the opposition to a rise of secular globalism among Western elites since the Wilson presidency, citing Obama-era pressure on African nations over laws against homosexual practice. Sandlin argues the United States was perhaps the first strictly propositional nation, resting on the Declaration of Independence and its God-given universal rights, as the Federalist number two suggests. He says opponents are really opposing the implicitly Christian founding and drifting toward blood and soil ideas linked to Nazi Germany, Franco's Spain and Hirohito's Japan. He concludes that any Christian nation must be propositional, since God's moral law binds every nation, citing Romans 3.
